bull.b: Randomized, double-blind Phase 2a data for foralumab showed statistically significant reductions in brain inflammation on PET imaging alongside clinically meaningful improvements in patient-reported fatigue, supporting a potential therapeutic effect versus placebo.
Favorable safety findings with full treatment completion and no drug-related serious adverse events reduce a key regulatory hurdle and support progression to larger trials.

Intranasal delivery of a fully human anti-CD3 antibody targets regulatory immune cells that can access brain lymphatic pathways, offering a differentiated approach to modulate central nervous system inflammation.

bear.b: Higher-dose arm did not show a significant imaging benefit, creating concern about an unclear dose-response relationship that could complicate dose selection for later studies.

Uncertain correlations between inflammatory markers, imaging readouts, and clinical neurodegeneration create the risk that observed biomarker improvements may not translate into meaningful patient outcomes.

Uncertainty exists whether the therapy will generate enough regulatory immune cells to convert imaging changes into durable clinical benefit, posing a core risk for late-stage development and approval.
